You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the DVD represented by the small central package in SOURCE visibly white in EDITED, when tracked using its position, scale, and surrounding scene context?
node.criteria: Locate the small central DVD package in SOURCE and examine its corresponding region in EDITED. Establish correspondence using position, footprint, nearby sand features, and surrounding scene context; retaining a rectangular outline is not required. Pass if these cues reliably identify the corresponding DVD item and its visible main surface is predominantly white rather than the source's dark appearance. Fail if the reliably corresponding item remains black or otherwise non-white. Return unknown if correspondence or color cannot be reliably established. Whiteness alone, or disappearance of the rectangular outline alone, is insufficient to decide. Do not use the right-side object or disc as a substitute for the central target.
node.binding: The target remains the small DVD package near the center of SOURCE, approximately x=258–304 and y=245–287. Track that source item across supported appearance/form changes; neither the right-side object nor an unrelated white disc is the target.
node.source_quote: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
node.endpoint: The central source DVD's corresponding edited item has a visibly white main surface.
node.necessity: The requested transformation concerns the source DVD, not arbitrary white objects. The central edited white item has nearly the same position and footprint as the source package, so correspondence must consider those concrete cues rather than requiring an unchanged rectangular form.

node_traces.evidence: The small DVD package is near the center in SOURCE, between the shoe and the dark object. In EDITED, a white disc-like item occupies nearly the same position and footprint, with matching nearby sand features; its main visible surface is white. The separate disc on the right is not used as the target.
